Alldergate, from which it run south-west by the back of Christ's Hospital and Old Norgeta, and passing behind the present prison of Newgate and Stationment Court, reached leadingte. Even that gate is provided western by Cock Court to the river Theg now Now Bridge Street, and trei minined at a fort called afterwards Barnani’s Castle. It was also thus covered by another wall along the bank of the Thames, which, however, was destroyed at a very remote period. The extent of the wall, exclusive of that by the side of the river, was two miles and one furling. That on the bank one mile and at total. The height of the walls was twenty-two feet, and they were defended by fifteen fifty thousand times. Through some of the were the great roads leading to the different parts of the kingdom. The preset way or the Valley Street, passed under Norgeta, and then turned towards the rivers where as farry connected with the road to Dover. The Hermin Street road passed under Griplegate. Another passed through Aldi- gate and moved by Bathan Green to the old fort over the river, and on towards Essex, Suffolk, and Norfolk. The process of time other roads were laid out, while the gates corresponding to them were erected and received the names of Bridgegate, Jedagree, Aldergata, Mororgate, Morogate, and the Potenz on Tower will.
